To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) radiocesium concentrations in reindeer/caribous and lichens in Alaska are generally low and 2) these data are consistent with the hypothesis that radiocesium concentrations are controlled by the rate of transfer of radiocesium between lichen and reindeer/cariboun.
The reindeer/cariboo food chain is an efficient pathway for the movement of radiocaesium (Cs 131) from the environment into man.

radiocesium concentrations in lichens in Alaska are typically less than 1.0 kBq/kg, that radiocesium in reindeer/caribous are generally less than 0.5 kBq/kg (wet weight), and that the radiocesium in caribous is less than 0,5 kBq/kg in the meat.
